title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 114
paragraphs: After these rites and many other charms for the river, at the Nine Ways in the land of the Edonians they crossed by the bridges, for they had found the Strymon already bridged. On being told that the place was called the Nine Ways, they buried alive there that number of boys and girls, children of the local inhabitants. Burying alive is a Persian custom: I am told that Amestris, the wife of Xerxes, when she had grown old, repaid her own life to the god who is said to dwell beneath the earth by burying twice seven children of Persian men of note.
